title: Noisy influence at one
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube and $i\in[n]$. Then $I_i^{(1)}(f)=I_i(f)$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation.
hypotheses_covered: coordinate i of the n-dimensional cube
Boolean function f of arity n
replaced:
At noise rate $\rho = 1$ the noisy influence coincides with the ordinary influence:
$\mathrm{Inf}_i^{1}[f] = \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$.
